import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Chvátal's Conjecture

*References:*

* [A Conjecture in Extremal Combinatorics](https://users.encs.concordia.ca/~chvatal/conjecture.html)
* [Chvátal's Conjecture and Correlation Inequalities](https://arxiv.org/abs/1608.08954)
-/

namespace Chvatal

variable {α : Type} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Nonempty α]

/-- A family F of sets is Decreasing if it is closed under taking subsets. -/
def Decreasing (F : Finset (Finset α)) : Prop :=
    ∀ A B : Finset α, B ⊆ A → A ∈ F → B ∈ F

/-- A family F of sets is Intersecting if each pair of members has nonempty intersection. -/
def Intersecting (F : Finset (Finset α)) : Prop :=
    ∀ A ∈ F, ∀ B ∈ F, A ∩ B ≠ ∅

/--
If F is a decreasing family of sets of some finite type α, then there is some element
x of α such that the family consisting of all members of F containing x is an intersecting
subfamily of F with maximal cardinality.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem exists_maximal_star :
    ∀ F : Finset (Finset α), Decreasing F →
        ∃ x : α, ∀ G, G ⊆ F → Intersecting G → G.card ≤ { A ∈ F | x ∈ A }.card := by
  sorry

reformulations.difference: The webpage counts {∅} as intersecting and excludes F = {∅} from the conjecture. Lean follows the arXiv paper’s all-pairs definition of intersecting and includes every decreasing F. It expresses maximum cardinality by requiring one star to bound every intersecting subfamily’s cardinality.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: A family intersecting under the webpage’s distinct-pair convention is either Lean-intersecting or exactly {∅}. For F ≠ {∅}, if {∅} ⊆ F, there is a nonempty A ∈ F. Any star bounding all Lean-intersecting subfamilies therefore has size at least one, by considering {A}, and also bounds the extra family {∅}. The converse implication is immediate. For F = {∅}, the only Lean-intersecting subfamily is empty, so the added case holds trivially on a nonempty ground type. Finally, the filtered star is automatically an intersecting subfamily of F, making the universal cardinality bound precisely the assertion that this star has maximum cardinality. Both equivalences were proved in /workspace/review/equivalence.lean without using the conjecture’s sorry.

sources_consulted: Friedgut–Kahn–Kalai–Keller, Chvátal’s Conjecture and Correlation Inequalities, arXiv:1608.08954v1, Introduction (definitions and Conjecture 1.1) and Proposition 2.1; LaTeX source read at https://arxiv.org/e-print/1608.08954
review.notes: Checked both definitions and the sole theorem, including elaborated parameters, quantifier order, subset and intersection semantics, filtering, and cardinalities. The Fintype and Nonempty assumptions are retained in the elaborated theorem. Empty-family and singleton-empty-family cases behave correctly. Computable tests in /workspace/review/inspect.lean exhaustively verified the proposition for all families on one, two, and three points. Both cited sources continue to present the general assertion as a conjecture.
